newsitem.title: UK: UPS management flying transatlantic flights.
newsitem.headline: UPS management flying transatlantic flights.

text.p: United Parcel Service Europe said management crews are flying its U.S. to Europe transatlantic services as the strike with its Teamsters union employees over a new five year contract enters its second day.
"The first management crews flew in yesterday afternoon," a company spokeswoman told Reuters from its European regional headquarters in Brussels.
The 2,000 unionised UPS pilots said when the strike started at 0400 gmt on Monday that they would stay off the job in sympathy with the strikers.

UPS operates three daily flights five days a week between the U.S and Europe. There is a daily Boeing 747 freighter flight from Philadelphia to Cologne -- the main UPS European hub -- with a return flight to Philadelphia.

The other two flights are operated by by Douglas DC-8 freighters with one flying from Louisville to its UK hub at East Midlands airport near Birmingham on to Cologne and back to Louisville. The other operates Louisville-Philadelphia-East Midlands-Cologne and returns via Newark to Louisville.
The company's intra-European and European domestic services remain unaffected by the strike and the 24,000 employees are working normally, a UPS Europe statement said on Tuesday.

However import traffic from the U.S. which arrives in Europe later today "is expected to be somewhat impacted " but the situation is seen having little effect on shipments bound for the U.S., the statement added.
"All international volume to and from the U.S. is receiving top priority," the company said.
Export volume levels in Europe yesterday continued at the strong level shown in previous weeks and are running above target levels, the company said.
